rationale: All three candidates measure identically (WNS -4.8352, TNS -303.7124, area 120706.0120, score -0.3615 — a -0.3615 improvement over the parent), so the choice is based on code clarity and maintainability. t2 is selected because: (1) it preserves the crucial explanatory comment block ('Same reason as crc_next above...') that documents why par_chain_out must be a named wire to keep the protected cdc_xfrm_from_look line unedited; (2) it provides the clearest level-by-level inline comments describing each reduction stage; (3) it uses conventional naming (par_l1 through par_l8) and separates wire declaration from assignment, maintaining consistency with the original par_chain_out pattern; (4) t1 is more compact but lacks the explanatory comment context; (5) t3 adds an unnecessary explicit passthrough (par_l0 = xd_q[511:0]) and loses the protective comment. Since functional equivalence and timing are identical across all three, code maintainability and clarity determine the best choice.

expected_vs_mechanical: No mechanical union was possible due to universal overlap. t2 provides not only the tree implementation but also preserves the critical architectural explanation: why par_chain_out is a wire rather than a direct assignment, which is enforced by the protection of the cdc_xfrm_from_look line. This context prevents future maintainers from 'optimizing' the code back into an unusable form.
equivalence_argument: The balanced binary tree computes the XOR of all 512 bits of xd_q over log₂(512) = 9 stages instead of 512. Each stage combines pairs with XOR: par_l1[i] = xd_q[2i] ⊕ xd_q[2i+1], then par_l2[i] = par_l1[2i] ⊕ par_l1[2i+1], etc. The final result par_l8[0] ⊕ par_l8[1] is the XOR of all 512 bits, identical to the original par_chain[512] which accumulated the same result serially. XOR is associative and commutative, so any binary tree computing all-bits-XOR is functionally equivalent. No reset logic is affected (all wires are combinational), and there is no width-extension concern (XOR preserves 1-bit width at each stage). Equivalence holds cycle-for-cycle.
